https://www.securitycouncilreport.org/mo.text: Monthly Forecast Monthly preview of issues in the Council Country and Regional Issues Publications on country-specific and regional issues in the Council Thematic and General Issues Council thematic and structural issues and peace making, keeping and building About the UN Security Council Background information on the Council, its subsidiary bodies and activities About SCR What's In Blue Past Publications Press Release Home Contact Resources Donate September 2026 Monthly Forecast Print Share On 5 August, the Security Council convened for a briefing on the Secretary-General’s 23rd biannual strategic-level report (S/2026/638) on the threat posed by the Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL/Da’esh) to international peace and security (S/PV.10205). The briefers were Oguljeren Niyazberdiyeva, the Chief of the Office of the Under-Secretary-General for Counter-Terrorism (OUSG) at the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism (UNOCT), and Carmen G. Cantor, the Deputy Executive Director of the Counter-Terrorism Committee Executive Directorate (CTED). On 6 August, the members of the Security Council issued a press statement condemning suicide terrorist attacks outside a police station in Kabal, Swat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province, Pakistan, on 2 August 2026 ( SC/16428 ). The attack resulted in the deaths of at least 16 Pakistani nationals. Responsibility for the attack was claimed by Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). On 6 August, the Security Council held an open briefing on the situation in South Sudan and the work of the UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) (S/PV.10206). Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of UNMISS Anita Kiki Gbeho briefed on the Secretary-General’s latest 90-day report (S/2026/640), which was circulated to Council members on 31 July and covered developments from 16 April to 15 July. Interim Chairperson of the Reconstituted Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission (RJMEC) Major General (retired) George Aggrey Owinow and Founder and President of the South Sudan Women’s Empowerment Network Lilian Riziq also briefed. Closed consultations followed the open briefing. On 27 August, Council members issued a press statement condemning in the strongest terms an attack by armed individuals on an UNMISS force-protection convoy in Jonglei State, which killed two peacekeepers and injured seven others. Council members stressed that attacks against UN peacekeepers may constitute war crimes under international law and called for a full, transparent, and immediate investigation. They also expressed deep alarm at persistent intercommunal and armed violence in Jonglei State and its impact on civilians, humanitarian workers, and peacekeepers. On 10 August, Latvia and the UK, with co-sponsorship from Ukraine, convened an Arria-formula meeting titled “Implementing international humanitarian law: prisoners of war, civilian detainees and foreign fighters, in the context of Russia’s war against Ukraine”. According to the concept note circulated by the co-organisers, the objective of the meeting was to draw attention to the treatment of Ukrainian prisoners of war and civilian detainees in Russian custody, alleged violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law, and what the note describes as the deceptive and coercive recruitment of foreign nationals into the Russian armed forces. The briefers included: Claudia Fuentes Julio, the Assistant Secretary-General for Human Rights and Head of the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) in New York; Leniie Umerova, a Crimean Tatar activist and human rights defender; Khuan Alberto Leyva Garsiya, a solider in the Ukrainian Armed Forces, who spent more than three years in Russian captivity before his release in August 2025; Oleg Gushchyn, a Ukrainian lawyer and legal expert with the Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War, a Ukrainian governmental body that coordinates state activities related to compliance with the Third and Fourth Geneva Conventions; and Sheida Kiran, a British-Turkish-Iranian documentary filmmaker who recently produced the film Into the Void: Putin’s Foreign Fighters , an investigation into the recruitment of foreign nationals to fight in the war. On 24 August, the Council held an open briefing on the situation in Ukraine (S/PV.10212). The meeting coincided with the anniversary of Ukraine’s declaration of independence in 1991 and marked four and a half years since Russia’s invasion of the country on 24 February 2022. The Council’s five European members—Denmark, France, Greece, Latvia, and the UK, collectively known as the “E5”—requested the meeting, which Denmark’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Lars Løkke Rasmussen, chaired. Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary DiCarlo and Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher briefed, while Iceland, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, and Ukraine participated in the meeting under rule 37 of the Council’s provisional rules of procedure. On 11 August, Council members discussed in closed consultations the 90-day report on the work of the 1718 Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) Sanctions Committee. Ordinarily, the chair of the 1718 Sanctions Committee would brief Council members on the report. At the time of writing, however, the chair had not been appointed, as members remained unable to agree on the allocation of the Council’s subsidiary bodies for 2026. Denmark, which held the Council presidency in August, therefore briefed members on the report, consistent with recent practice. On 7 August, Security Council members issued a press statement expressing concern at heightened tensions in Yemen ( SC/16429 ). The statement condemned “unauthorized landings of aircraft at Sana’a International Airport on 3 July and Hudaydah Airport on 13 July, without permissions and clearances from the Government of Yemen in violation of international civil aviation rules, and missile attacks launched by the Houthis against Saudi Arabia since 13 July, as well as commercial vessels since 22 July”. On 13 August, the Security Council held a briefing on the situation in Yemen ( S/PV.10208 ). UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg and Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher briefed. Yemen participated in the meeting under rule 37 of the Council’s provisional rules of procedure. On 18 August, Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of the UN Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) Hanna Serwaa Tetteh briefed the Council on recent political, security, and humanitarian developments in the country and the Secretary-General’s latest report on UNSMIL (S/2026/661). While noting progress on the political process and UNSMIL-facilitated roadmap, Tetteh noted that Libya continues to face numerous challenges on the domestic front. She expressed concern over the fragile security situation along the country’s western coast and recent power and water disruptions across the country. On 19 August, the Security Council held its annual open debate on working methods (S/PV.10210 and Resumption I). The open debate was convened under the agenda item “Implementation of the note by the President of the Security Council ( S/2024/507 )”, referring to the most recent version of the comprehensive compendium of Council working methods. Shamala Kandiah Thompson, the Executive Director of Security Council Report, briefed. Besides Council members, 49 member states participated in the meeting. Among the issues raised were the need for greater transparency in the process of selecting the next Secretary-General, the lack of agreement in the appointment of subsidiary body chairs, and penholderships. On 20 August, following the closed consultations on the work of the 1718 Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) Sanctions Committee, Council members discussed the situation in Georgia under “any other business” (AOB). The E5 requested the meeting to mark the 18th anniversary of the 2008 Russia-Georgia war. Assistant Secretary-General for the Middle East, Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific in the Departments of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs and Peace Operations (DPPA-DPO) Mohamed Khaled Khiari briefed. On 25 August, the Security Council held a high-level open debate on conflict-related food insecurity under the agenda item “Maintenance of international peace and security” ( S/PV.10213 , Resumption I , and Resumption 2 ). The meeting, titled “Food under fire: the Security Council’s role in mitigating global and local food rises” was a signature event of Denmark’s August Council presidency and was chaired by Denmark’s Minister for Foreign Affairs Lars Løkke Rasmussen. Secretary-General António Guterres briefed. He expressed concern at the record numbers of people facing food insecurity worldwide due to conflict, while urging Council members to use all tools available to prevent and end conflicts, including resolution 2417, to mitigate the impact of conflict on food systems. Carl Skau, the Acting Executive Director of the World Food Programme (WFP), also briefed the Council and spoke about several situations where conflict and hunger are in a vicious cycle. He also warned of a new dimension in which certain conflict zones—such as those in the Black Sea, the Red Sea, and the Strait of Hormuz—have created choke points that have impacted food and energy supplies and threatened to push tens of millions more into hunger. Perrine Benoist, the Co-CEO of Action Against Hunger , representing the Coalition Against Conflict and Hunger , briefed as well. On 28 August, Security Council members held closed consultations on Lebanon. France, the penholder on Lebanon, called the meeting in light of the deteriorating situation in the south of the country and to begin discussion of possible arrangements after the termination of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL). Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary DiCarlo and Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations Jean-Pierre Lacroix briefed. On 28 August, at Russia’s request, Security Council members discussed the death of Ratko Mladić under “any other business” (AOB) following the closed consultations on Lebanon. Mladić was serving a life sentence at the UN Detention Unit in The Hague after being convicted by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) for genocide, crimes against humanity, and violations of the laws or customs of war committed during the 1992-1995 conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH). There were no briefers. https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/141936.text: Two Latvian nationals arrested after hole found in fence at UK military base Military police began investigating after discovering an abandoned vehicle near the base on Wednesday evening Two Latvian men arrested inside a British military base used for US and NATO intelligence operations have been released on bail as police continue a national security investigation. According to The Guardian, the men, aged 32 and 26, were detained at RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire at around 2:00 AM on Thursday. Military police began investigating after discovering an abandoned vehicle near the base on Wednesday evening. Officers later found a a small hole in the perimeter fence before locating the two men inside the facility. Both suspects, who live in the UK, were initially arrested on suspicion of trespassing at a prohibited site and causing criminal damage. They were subsequently arrested on suspicion of entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK under the National Security Act 2023. The men have since been released on bail under strict conditions. Commander Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said investigators were examining why the men entered the base and whether criminal activity was involved. Police said there was currently no evidence linking the incident to a separate security concern near RAF Fairford in September. Officers have searched two properties in the Peterborough area and seized the abandoned vehicle. Trump demands Rep. https://hvg.hu/kultura/20261114_hazai-bu.text: Az HBO is felült a true crime-népszerűségi vonatra, és milyen jól tette. Az igazság mániákusai kifejezetten izgalmasan mutat be két a rendszerváltás után az egész országot megrázó bűntényt, Farkas Helga elrablását és a Magda Marinko nevéhez köthető sorozatgyilkosságot. A lányt soha nem találták meg, a Magda Marinko-ügyben pedig épp a legszörnyűbb fejezet maradt felderítetlen. Az elmúlt években különösen népszerűek lettek világszerte az úgynevezett true crime-ok, azaz a valós bűnügyeket bemutató alkotások, legyenek azok dokumentumfilmek, játékfilmek, sorozatok. A népszerűségüknek jót tett az is, hogy a bűnügyeket így-úgy bemutató korábbi, meglehetősen gagyi filmes elemeket felvonultató mozgóképek helyét mára egyértelműen átvették a kifejezetten mívesen, gyönyörű képekkel, izgalmas dramaturgiával elmesélt történetek. Ezekben a nézőket egyszerre vonzza a rejtély, a lélektani háttér, a nyomozás folyamata és mindemellett az a talán nyugtalanító felismerés is, hogy a történetek nem forgatókönyvírók fantáziájából születtek, hanem valódi emberek életében történtek meg. Azaz a klasszikus krimik izgalmát kínálják a valóság hitelességével. Az HBO új, magyar gyártású dokumentumsorozata, Az igazság mániákusai ebbe a műfajba kapcsolódik be, méghozzá úgy, hogy nem elsősorban a bűnelkövetők, hanem az őket üldöző nyomozók kerülnek a középpontba. Szajki-Vörös Adél és Szajki Péter sorozatában a történeteket olyan szakemberek mesélik el, akik maguk is részt vettek az egykori nyomozásokban. A keretét egy nyugdíjas vacsoratársaság adja. A házigazda Tóth Ernő nyugalmazott rendőr alezredes vendégeivel, Kovács Lajos, Kőrösi János, Krispán István és Petőfi Attila ismert, ma már nyugdíjas nyomozókkal („a rendszerváltás előtti rendőrség gyerekei” – jellemzik magukat), illetve Illisz László bűnügyi újságíróval beszélget a pörkölt fölött az egykor általuk felderített, vagy épphogy nem teljesen felderített ügyekről. A sorozat ezek közül kettő olyat fejt ki bővebben, amelyek a rendszerváltás zavaros időszaka körüli Magyarország közvéleményét igencsak megrázták. Mind a kettő felderítésében van hiányérzete a szakembereknek. Az ügyek bemutatása során nem maradunk a vacsoraasztalnál: az egykor érintett nyomozók saját emlékeiken, tapasztalataikon és szakmai döntéseiken keresztül idézik fel a múltat úgy, hogy visszamennek a nyomozások főbb helyszíneire, eredeti hangfelvételeket mutatnak az emberrablók telefonjaiból, és megszólaltatnak érintett tanúkat, rendőröket, ügyvédeket is. Szinte krimiszerűen, mozaikokból összerakva tudhatja meg a néző, hogy mi történt az adott ügyekben, és azt is, hogyan gondolkodtak anno a nyomozók, amikor még nem volt internet, nem voltak digitális adatbázisok, és nem voltak adottak a mai technikai lehetőségek. Amikor még a megfigyelés, az emberismeret, a logikus következtetés és a kitartó munka (valamint az ügyes trükkök) sokszor többet értek minden modern technológiánál. Az első epizód középpontjában a 17 éves orosházi Farkas Helga 1991. júniusi eltűnése áll. Az ügyet emberrablásként kezelték, hiszen a lány gazdag vállalkozó apjától komoly váltságdíjat követeltek telefonon (ezeknek az eredeti felvételét is hallhatjuk a filmben). Az eset különösen nagy visszhangot váltott ki akkoriban, hiszen, mint Kovács Lajos, egykor az ORFK Életvédelmi Osztályának, illetve az úgynevezett „döglött ügyek” alosztályának vezetője elmondja, ilyen emberrablásos esettel még nem volt dolga a magyar rendőrségnek. A rendszerváltás utáni Magyarországon egy ilyen bűncselekmény egyszerre jelentett rendőrségi, társadalmi és médiabeli szenzációt. A műfaji sajátosságokhoz illően szép lassan építkező filmben nagytotálok és a fontos helyszíneket bemutató képek váltakoznak a rendszerváltás idején készült archívokkal, az érintettek interjúfelvételeivel, és nagyon ízlésesen adagolt, csak fel-felvillanó (és a műfajban sokszor megszokottakhoz képest itt egyáltalán nem hatásvadász) akciójelenetekkel. A legemlékezetesebbek talán azok a gyönyörű drónfelvételek, amelyek a viharsarki végtelen pusztát pásztázzak, azt, ahol az emberrablás történt, és ami a lány holttestét vélhetően máig rejti valahol. Az ugyanis soha nem került elő, mint ahogy az emberrablás körülményei és a történtek számos részlete továbbra is megválaszolatlan kérdéseket hagyott maga után. Egy olasz kisvárosban bukkantak rá arra a férfira, aki több mint két és fél évtizeddel ezelőtt elrabolhatta és vélhetően megölte a fiatal lányt – írta a Magyar Nemzet. Izgalmasan mutatja be a film, hogy a Matávtól megkapott telefonhívások felvételeiből, a tanúvallomásokból, a helyszínek bejárásából és egyéb gyanús nyomokból hogyan találtak rá a feltételezett elkövetőkre. És nem hallgatja el azt sem, hogy az ügy teljes felderítésében kudarcot vallott a rendőrség. A második epizód a Magda Marinko nevéhez kötődő gyilkosságsorozat felderítését idézi fel. (A témában egyébként nemrég jött ki egy háromrészes dokumentumfilmsorozat is A Kegyetlen – Magda Marinko rémtörténete címmel, aki igazán árnyalt benyomásokat szeretne az ügyről, érdemes mindkét alkotást megnéznie.) A szerb Magda Marinko a kilencvenes évek első felében Magyarországon és a környező országokban elkövetett súlyos bűncselekmények miatt vált hírhedtté. Nevéhez összesen 16 emberölést kötöttek. Az ügyek hátterében a korabeli délszláv és magyar alvilág kapcsolatai, valamint a rendszerváltás utáni időszak bizonytalan közbiztonsági viszonyai is megjelentek. A nyomozás is rendkívül összetett volt, hiszen a bűncselekmények több helyszínhez és országhoz kapcsolódtak. A hatóságoknak apró nyomokból, tanúvallomásokból és egymást kiegészítő információkból kellett felépíteniük az elkövetőhöz vezető bizonyítékláncot. Mi is bejárjuk a nyomozókkal a kecskeméti, orosházi gyilkosságok helyszínét, és ahhoz a szegedi házhoz is ellátogatunk, ahol 1994. január 23-án éjjel a gyerekekkel együtt végeztek ki egy cukrászcsaládot. Ez utóbbi gyilkosságot, noha a nyomozók szerint ők egyértelműen felderítették, a bíróság nem varrta Magda Marinko nyakába. Bár a francia idegenlégiót és a délszláv-háborút megjárt kegyetlen bűnözőt végül elfogták, és életfogytiglani szabadságvesztésre ítélték, a szegedi cukrászcsalád tragédiája máig hivatalosan felderítetlen ügy. A film dramaturgiailag és képileg is hasonlóan (zseniálisan lassan, és szép képekkel) építkezik, mint a Farkas Helga-ügyet bemutató első rész, igaz, itt szerepet kap – teljesen feleslegesen – egy madár is, amelynek szemszögéből látjuk többször a pusztai tájat. A zsákmányra leső ragadozó ugyanakkor túl didaktikus, nem erősíti, hanem gyengíti a sztorit. Az eljáró bíróval, ügyésszel és saját védőjével sem volt hajlandó kommunikálni. Egy a sajtó által is agyontárgyalt, lezárt, feldolgozott ügyről szóló true crime-filmről is lehet spoilerezni. Ezt nem tesszük meg, de annyit elárulunk, hogy olyan izgalmas részletek is kiderülnek a beszámolókból, hogy mi volt a szerepe a felderítésben egy papírfecninek, vagy egy hosszú, a végére komoly dulakodássá alakult kihallgatásnak, és hogy miért kellett építeni külön Magda Marinkónak egy speciális zárkát. A műfaj kedvelőinek kötelező néznivaló Az igazság mániákusai . Aki nem ismeri a rendszerváltás körüli zavaros időszak megrázó bűnügyeit, vagy ismeri, de újra el szeretne gondolkodni azokon, azoknak pedig erősen ajánlott. 5 071 632 000 forint, 2 658 350 euró, 1 257 100 dollár.

https://www.dw.com/en/apec-summit-trump-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PWTX Prefer DW on Google Putin, Xi and Trump have met for highly anticipated trilateral talks Image: Win McNamee/REUTERS Advertisement Skip next section What you need to know What you need to know Three-way talks between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping have finished The talks took place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit held in China's Shenzhen Trump was greeted by Xi at the airport before greeting Putin in their first face-to-face in over a year Trump held bilateral talks with 'friend' Putin as well as separate talks with Xi ahead of the main event The wars in Ukraine and Iran, as well as nuclear arms controls, were on top of the agenda for the trilateral talks Here are the biggest headlines from the APEC summit and Trump 's Asia tour on Thursday, November 19: Skip next section Analysis: No more than crumbs of comfort on nuclear weapons 11/19/2026 November 19, 2026 Analysis: No more than crumbs of comfort on nuclear weapons Richard Walker Chief International Editor Donald Trump’s big theme going into the three-way summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin was "denuclearization" — saying in his opening remarks that they were "uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth." But there are no signs that that will happen. China has long resisted US calls for three-way talks on arms control, and Xi’s reported call during the summit for a world without nuclear weapons was merely a reaffirmation of longstanding policy. In fact, as signatories of the global Nonproliferation Treaty, all nuclear states are committed to pursuing nuclear disarmament. So the fact that the final "Heads of State Declaration toward Peace" fails to indicate any steps towards disarmament could be read by critics as just the latest failure to take that seriously. China is engaged in a rapid buildup of its nuclear forces, from warheads to advanced theater missiles; Russia has made repeated threats to use nuclear weapons in its war in Ukraine; and the United States, despite Trump’s calls for "denuclearization," is working on as many as four new theater missiles of its own to try to catch up with the other two in what could be the decisive nukes of this era. Neither should the Declaration’s reaffirmation of the Reagan-Gorbachev mantra "a nuclear war can never be won and must never be fought" be seen as much source of comfort — all three states last retook this oath in January 2022, just weeks before Putin launched his war. And yet — the Declaration does have some crumbs of comfort for anyone seeking positive nuclear news. It says the three powers will "conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks." Possible areas for progress here would include commitments to notify other states when doing test launches of nuclear missiles (China has no such commitment), or keeping AI out of nuclear command and control (so far only the US and China have a very broad commitment that only humans should order a launch). This would be the lowest of low-hanging fruit — after all, does anyone want AI to launch nuclear weapons? – but an optimist might say, it would be better than nothing. Let’s see. Edited by: Rob Turner https://p.dw.com/p/5PdlX Skip next section European officials invited to Moscow to discuss involvement in Ukraine talks, says Putin 11/19/2026 November 19, 2026 European officials invited to Moscow to discuss involvement in Ukraine talks, says Putin Putin said the US has urged Russia to involve Europeans in talks to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine Image: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Russian Presidential Press and Information Office/TASS/IMAGO Russian President Vladimir Putin said European officials have been invited to Moscow to discuss the potential structure of talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine. "The American side is urging us to agree to the involvement of the Europeans ... Through diplomatic channels, we suggested to the Europeans to come to Moscow. And after that we will decide in what format the talks can continue," Putin said at a press conference in China. "We understand that discussing issues linked to security in Europe is pointless without the Europeans," Putin added. For months, European politicians have emphasized that they should be present at any talks on the future of Ukraine. The Russian leader also said it would be unacceptable for there to be military cooperation between Ukraine and the EU and that included any potential deployment of troops to the country. "Military cooperation in any form is, of course, a problem," Putin told reporters. Allies of Ukraine, the "Coalition of the Willing," are meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy today in Berlin. Edited by: Sean Sinico https://p.dw.com/p/5PdfO Skip next section What do we know about agreements at the trilateral summit? 11/19/2026 November 19, 2026 What do we know about agreements at the trilateral summit? Timothy Jones The highly anticipated three-way talks between US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday have ended. Ahead of the talks, Trump said they would be about "all problems that are being discussed in the world" Here are quotes from the leaders and from a joint statement on the topics they addressed: Nuclear arms Trump: "The United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth and also to lessen the risk of those weapons being used." Xi: "A nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. Every effort must be made to prevent nuclear war, adhere to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, and maintain global strategic stability." International Criminal Court and UN In a joint statement reported by Chinese state media and the Kremlin, the leaders agreed that "the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction." The leaders also "acknowledged the vital importance of the principle of state consent and the respect for (diplomatic) immunity enjoyed by state officials." The statement added that all three countries were "committed" to advancing reform of the United Nations. Energy The joint statement said the countries "plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products." It reaffirmed "the importance of the stable flow of energy." Neither the war in Ukraine nor the conflict in Iran were directly mentioned at the talks, according to the Russian and Chinese accounts. Edited by: Sean Sinico https://p.dw.com/p/5PdUY Skip next section China and Russia report on 'peace declaration' from trilateral summit 11/19/2026 November 19, 2026 China and Russia report on 'peace declaration' from trilateral summit Timothy Jones Chinese state media and Russian officials have been summarizing a declaration issued by the US, Chinese and Russian presidents at their trilateral summit, which US President Donald Trump billed as history-making. According to the accounts of what was dubbed a "peace declaration," the three leaders reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be ⁠won ​and must ​never be fought. The three presidents of major nuclear powers are quoted as saying they would hold a dialogue on the reduction of nuclear risks and the prevention of nuclear proliferation. The three men also "reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows," saying they plan to up the production and supply of refined petroleum products, according to the Chinese Xinhua news agency.
